reason: This passage describes the Golden Calf incident (Exodus 32). The Hebrews demonstrate clear ingratitude and unfaithfulness to Yahweh by creating and worshiping an idol while Moses receives the Torah on Mount Sinai. The text explicitly describes the people as 'פָרֻעַ' (parua - breaking loose/uncontrolled), indicating they have abandoned their covenant obligations to the God who delivered them from Egypt. Additionally, the people showed disrespect to their leader Moses by pressuring Aaron to create the idol in his absence. The subsequent divine punishment through the Levites killing approximately 3,000 men underscores the severity of this ingratitude and rebellion against both Yahweh and the established leadership.
